title: Handling and Assessment of Human Primary Prostate Organoid Culture
protocol: Collect necessary materials for seeding epithelial cells: human primary prostate epithelial cells (PrE), matrix gel on ice, 96-well microplate, keratinocyte serum-free media (KSFM) on ice, charcoal stripped fetal bovine serum (FBS), and dihydrotestosterone (DHT).
Prepare KSFM-based organoid media by combining 47.5 mL of KSFM with 2.5 mL of charcoal stripped FBS and DHT to a final concentration of 10 nM DHT.
Gently mix cold KSFM-based organoid media with ice-cold matrix gel to obtain a 50% matrix gel mixture by slowly pipetting up and down, avoiding bubbles.
Pre-wet a pipette tip in cold media.
Transfer 40-50 μL of 50% matrix gel onto the bottom of each well of a 96-well plate.
Coat the bottom of the well to form a base layer.
Place the 96-well plate into a 37 °C incubator for 30–45 min to solidify the base layer.
Mix epithelial cells suspended in KSFM-based organoid media with matrix gel to achieve a final concentration of 100-1,000 cells/100 μL and 33% matrix gel.
Plate epithelial cells on top of base layers using 100 μL of 33% matrix gel/cell mixture per well.
Place the 96-well plate in a 37 °C incubator for 30–45 min to allow the matrix gel to solidify.
Gently add 100 μL of KSFM-based organoid media on top of cells by pipetting slowly against the edge of the well.
Change the media every 2-3 days.
Pipette against the side of the well with space between the media and matrix gel.
Remove 50 μL of media.
Replace removed media with 50 μL of fresh media.
Warm neutral protease and Hanks' balanced salt solution (HBSS) in a 37 °C water bath.
Carefully remove media from wells without disrupting the matrix gel.
Add ~200 μL of neutral protease to each well at a ~1:2 ratio of matrix gel:neutral protease.
Incubate for 20 min at 37 °C.
Mechanically dissociate the matrix gel:neutral protease mixture by pipetting up and down.
Incubate the mixture for another 20 min at 37 °C.
Transfer the neutral protease-matrix gel-cell mixture to a microcentrifuge tube or conical tube, depending on volume.
Centrifuge at 300 x g for 3-5 min to pellet cells.
Resuspend organoids in 1 mL of warm cell-dissociation enzymes and incubate at 37 °C for 10–15 min to dissociate the organoids into single cells.
Wash once with 5 mL of HBSS.
Acquire whole-well z-stack images using a transmitted light inverted microscope with a motorized X/Y scanning stage.
Adjust the focal position to the bottom of the well and begin focusing upward until encountering the first organoid, setting this as the bottom z-plane.
Continue focusing upward until reaching the last organoid in focus, setting this as the top z-plane.
Ensure that the set z-range captures all organoids within each well and adjust if necessary.
Capture 15–35 z-planes per well for greater resolution.
Save z-stack images for downstream analysis.
Analyze images using image software with freeform drawing capabilities.
Open a single z-plane image set from step 3.1.4.
If needed, tile the images taken at each individual z-plane into a single, whole-well image.
Save the new image as a separate file.
Repeat this process for each z-plane acquired.
Using image software, open the whole-well image for every z-plane from a single well.
Create an extended depth of field (EDF) image from the stack of z-planes.
Set the pixel scale of the software to the scale bar of the image that is being measured.
Use the freeform drawing tool of the image software to trace the perimeter of every organoid in the well.
Obtain measurement metrics for traced organoid perimeters from the image software.
Recommended parameters are area, circularity, and maximum/minimum radius ratio.
Area is calculated from the polygon defined by the organoid’s perimeter.
Circularity is the ratio of the area of the organoid to the area of a circle with a diameter equal to the organoid’s maximum ferret, where 0 is less circular and 1 is more circular.
Maximum/minimum radius ratio is the ratio between the maximum radius and minimum radius of the traced organoid.
Prepare two microcentrifuge tubes of 2% agar solution.
Incubate the 2% agar solutions in a water bath or on a heat block at 100–110 °C to maintain them in liquid form.
Add 1-2 drops of histologic marking dye to one of the 2% agar solutions.
Mix well.
Warm the histology gel in a water bath or heat block at 55–65 °C.
Create molds using pipette tips that hold approximately 50 μL.
Wrap an ice pack with tape and adhere molds to the tape to create a cold block.
Remove the plunger from a 1 cc insulin syringe to create a plunger for embedding.
Embed organoids in a histology gel plug for processing.
Re-suspend the organoid pellet in 30–50 μL of liquid histology gel.
Mix gently by pipetting up and down slowly.
Transfer the histology gel/organoid mixture into a mold on the cold block.
Allow the specimen to cool and solidify into a plug.
Use a plunger to push the plug out of the small mold and into the larger mold.
Pipette clear 2% agar around the plug to fill the larger mold.
Pipette histologic dye-tinted 2% agar on top of the plug to denote the top of the sample.
Once cooled, use a plunger to transfer the plug into a histology cassette.
Label the cassette using a pencil and place cassette into 10% NBF for fixation overnight.
Transfer the cassette from 10% NBF to 70% histological grade EtOH.
Process the histology gel plug using a pre-set biopsy protocol on a processor, if available.

If preset is not available, input the following sequence and lengths: 70% EtOH for 6 min, 70% EtOH for 10 min, 80% EtOH for 10 min, 95% EtOH 2 times for 10 min, 100% EtOH 3 times for 10 min, xylene 3 times for 15 min, and paraffin 3 times for 15 min.
Embed the histology gel plug with the colored portion facing up.
Section the FFPE histology gel blocks.

Collect necessary supplies: FFPE histology gel blocks, histology pen, tissue float water bath, ice bucket with ice, microtome, microtome blades, embedding workstation, positively charged microscope slides, and laboratory oven.
Fill water bath until very full and set to 40 °C.
Pre-warm laboratory oven to 45–50 °C.
Prepare an ice bucket by filling it with ice and adding water to create an ice-water slurry.
Chill the blocks on ice until they are very cold.
Insert a block into microtome cassette clamp, add the blade to the knife holder, and unlock any protective locking measures on the machine.
Trim the face of the paraffin block at a 10 µm thickness.
Stop trimming once a section containing the plug area emerges.
Lock the microtome rotor and transfer the block back onto the ice to chill.
Move the blade to a new, unused portion.
Transfer the block back to the clamp.
Unlock the machine and begin trimming at 5 μm per section.
Using tweezers, transfer the section to the 40 °C water bath and allow the section to spread out.
Dip the slide vertically into the water to transfer the section onto a slide.
Visualize the section under microscope.
Circle the area around the section on the back of slide with a histology pen and bake overnight at 45–50 °C if organoids are present.
Proceed to H&E staining, immunohistochemical staining, or immunofluorescent staining as per the kit instructions.
Collect baked slide from step 4.
Immerse slide in xylene (3 dips, 5 minutes each).
Dip slide in 100% EtOH (2 dips, 3 minutes each).
Dip slide in 95% EtOH (2 dips, 3 minutes each).
Dip slide in 70% EtOH (2 dips, 3 minutes each).
Dip slide in deionized water (DI H2O) (2 dips, 3 minutes each).
Fill staining dish with antigen retrieval solution.
Pre-heat decloaking chamber to 100 °C.
Immerse slides into pre-heated staining dish.
Incubate slides for 5–10 min at 100°C.
Allow decloaking chamber to sit for 20 min before opening lid.
Place the slide dish under running DI H2O to rinse the slides for 5 min.
Remove the slides from the staining dish.
Draw a circle around the sample with a hydrophobic barrier pen.
Lay the slide on the humidity chamber.
Block non-specific antibody staining by applying 5% NHS with 0.1% non-ionic detergent in PBS to the hydrophobic circle around the sample.
Wash slides in coplins filled with PBS three times for 5 minutes each.
Add first-degree antibodies diluted in 1% BSA with 0.3% non-ionic detergent in PBS to the hydrophobic circle around the sample.
Incubate samples for 1 hour at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C in a humidity chamber.
Wash slides in coplins filled with PBS three times for 5 minutes each.
Add second-degree antibody diluted in 1% BSA with 0.3% non-ionic detergent in PBS to the hydrophobic circle around the sample.
Incubate samples for 1 hour at room temperature in a humidity chamber.
Wash slides in coplins filled with PBS three times for 5 minutes each.
Add DAPI, diluted according to manufacturer’s specifications, in 1% BSA with 0.3% non-ionic detergent in PBS to the hydrophobic circle around the sample.
Incubate samples for 2–5 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Wash slides in coplins filled with PBS three times for 5 minutes each.
Mount the slides with antifade mounting media and coverslip.
Visualize results under a microscope.

Collect supplies including chamber slide or confocal dish, PBS, fixative, 50 mM NH4Cl in PBS, 0.1% non-ionic detergent in PBS, 5% NHS with 0.1% non-ionic detergent in PBS, 1% BSA with 0.3% non-ionic detergent in PBS, primary and secondary antibodies of interest, and counterstains.
Remove as much media as possible without disrupting the organoid culture by pipetting against the side of the well.
Draw up one drop (25–50 μL) of matrix gel containing the organoids using a trimmed 1,000 μL pipette tip pre-wet with media or PBS.
Dispense the drawn matrix gel drop onto the middle of a chamber slide well or confocal dish.
Aspirate excess media and matrix gel from the chamber slide with a fine-tip pipette (10–200 μL).
Replace media in the parent culture with warm KSFM-based media if organoids remain.
Place the chamber slide in a 37 °C incubator for 30–45 min.
Pipette slowly to wash organoids with 200 μL of 1x PBS for 5 min at RT while gently shaking.
Remove the 1x PBS and fix with 200 μL of 4% paraformaldehyde for 30 min at RT while gently shaking.
Ensure that the matrix gel appears clear after this step.
Wash twice with 200 μL of 1x PBS for 5 min while gently shaking.
Quench autofluorescence with 200 μL of 50 mM NH4Cl in 1x PBS for 30 min at RT while gently shaking.
Remove NH4Cl and wash twice with 200 μL of 1x PBS for 5 min while gently shaking.
Permeabilize organoids in 200 μL of 0.1% non-ionic detergent-100 in 1x PBS for 30 min at RT while gently shaking.
Remove the 0.1% non-ionic detergent-100 in 1x PBS and wash twice with 200 μL of 1x PBS for 5 min while gently shaking.
Block with 5% NHS with 200 μL of 0.1% non-ionic detergent X-100 in PBS and incubate for 60 min at RT while gently shaking.
Remove the blocking buffer and wash twice with 200 μL of 1x PBS for 5 min while gently shaking.
Dilute the 1° antibody in 1% BSA with 0.3% Triton X-100 in 1x PBS and add to 200 μL of the chamber slide, then incubate for 1–3 days at 4 °C.
Remove the 1° antibody and wash twice with 200 μL of 1x PBS for 5 min while gently shaking.
Dilute the 2° antibody in 1% BSA with 0.3% Triton X-100 in 1x PBS and add to 200 μL of the chamber slide, then incubate for 1–3 days at 4 °C in the dark.
Remove the 2° antibody and wash twice with 200 μL of 1x PBS for 5 min while gently shaking.
Counterstain the actin with phalloidin and the nucleus with DAPI or Hoescht, diluted according to the manufacturer’s recommendations in 1% BSA with 0.3% Triton-X in 1x PBS.
Add 200 μl of staining solution to chamber slide.
Incubate at RT for 40 min in the dark.
Mount in 200 μl of fresh 1x PBS or mounting media and image immediately.
Carefully remove 50 μl of media from organoids.
Replace with 50 μl of 20 μm 2x working EdU solution by pipetting against the side of well, leaving space between media and matrix gel.
Incubate at 4 °C for 1–3 days for EdU incorporation.
Remove PBS and fix with 200 μL of 3.7% paraformaldehyde for 30 minutes at room temperature while gently shaking.
Ensure the matrix gel appears clear after fixing.
Remove the fixative and wash twice with 200 μL of 1x PBS for 5 minutes while gently shaking.
Remove PBS and add 200 μL of 0.5% non-ionic detergent-100 in 1x PBS for 30 minutes at room temperature while gently shaking.
Prepare a 1x fluorescent reaction cocktail according to the manufacturer’s specifications.
Remove 0.5% non-ionic detergent-100 and wash twice with 200 μL of 3% BSA in 1x PBS for 5 minutes while gently shaking.
Add reaction cocktail and incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Remove the fluorescent reaction cocktail and wash once with 200 μL of 3% BSA in 1x PBS for 5 minutes while gently shaking.
Counterstain and mount by following steps 6.21–6.22 (Figure 3D).
